operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: WHO Expert Panel Ends Ervebo Ring Vaccination — ChAdOx1 BDBV and Remdesivir Designated Priority Candidates
heroSubtitle: A WHO expert panel convened on May 28 issued a landmark ruling that rVSV-ZEBOV (Ervebo) must NOT be used outside research settings for BDBV efficacy assessment — effectively halting the off-label ring vaccination campaign currently underway in Ituri Province and Kampala. ChAdOx1 BDBV (Oxford/Serum Institute) remains the highest-priority vaccine candidate, with Phase 1 human trials possible within 2–3 months pending additional animal data; MBP134, Maftivimab, and remdesivir were designated priority therapeutics for confirmed-case trials. As of May 29, CDC confirmed 132 total lab-confirmed cases (DRC 125 + Uganda 7), with DRC MoH reconciling its suspected count to 906 after removing non-cases. The Uganda 4-week DRC border closure entered its second day. The 25+ escaped Mongbwalu ETU patients remain unaccounted, DRC contact tracing coverage remains below 45%, and ring vaccination strategy is now in flux amid the expert panel ruling.
footerNote: Data sourced from WHO Situation Reports, CDC Ebola Situation Summary, DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE), Uganda Ministry of Health, ECDC, MSF field reports, Oxford University Jenner Institute, CEPI, and U.S. State Department. Case counts and CFR figures are rapidly evolving.
